lead.hed: Philippine, Japanese, and U.S. ships trained together inside the Philippine exclusive economic zone
lead.insight: U.S. Pacific Command said the Armed Forces of the Philippines, the Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force, and the U.S. Coast Guard ran a multilateral Maritime Cooperative Activity in the Philippine exclusive economic zone on Oct. 24. It was the 14th such activity of 2026, a five-day drill on maritime domain awareness, maritime law enforcement, and search and rescue. Ships in the formation included Philippine Coast Guard patrol vessel BRP Suluan, Philippine Navy frigate BRP Diego Silang, Japanese destroyer JS Kirisame, and U.S. Coast Guard cutter USCGC Bertholf. The official still shows those three ships together at sea on Oct. 23.
lead.image_credit: Courtesy photo · DVIDS 10045890 · Public domain · BRP Suluan, USCGC Bertholf, and JS Kirisame in formation during a Maritime Cooperative Activity, Philippine exclusive economic zone, Oct. 23, 2026.

political.hed: Heritage says the American Jewish story tests the Founders' design
political.insight: Thursday's Heritage report says the American Jewish experience is one of the clearest historical tests of the Founders' design, and that the argument matters as the country marks 250 years amid renewed antisemitism and civic fragmentation. The piece is argument. It does not cite a new statute.

political.hed: American Reformer says the fertility drop is a friendship problem, not a married-couple one
political.insight: Wednesday's American Reformer essay by Lyman Stone says the U.S. fertility rate fell from 2.1 to 1.6 children per woman since 2007. Stone writes that married couples are not foregoing children more than they did in 2007, and that married fertility has slipped only slightly. The rest of the argument sits behind a subscription wall.

political.hed: Law & Liberty reads Lois Lowry's latest as a world that has lost its stories
political.insight: Friday's Law & Liberty review says Lois Lowry's Building 903 projects readers into a desiccated, post-literate world. The reviewer ties the new book to Lowry's earlier children's fiction, including a death scene in Autumn Street that still reads like a battlefield. It is a book review. It does not cite a floor vote.

tech.hed: The Army opened a sandbox so vendors can get software scanned before it reaches the network
tech.insight: The Army said Friday it launched Project Gatekeeper, a testing sandbox for commercial software. Acting chief information officer Gabe Chiulli said companies used to navigate ad-hoc routes just to get code evaluated. Gatekeeper lets developers submit code and containerized applications into isolated environments and get automated security feedback in near-real time.

tech.hed: The Air Force wants cameras and software to grade aerial refueling crews after the pass
tech.insight: Defense News reported Friday that the Air Force wants artificial intelligence to watch aerial refueling from cameras on the tankers and give crews a hot-wash afterward. The request is in an Air Force small-business solicitation. It is a want, not a fielded system.

tech.hed: Washington told the U.N. a Russian satellite closed on a U.S.-registered radar craft
tech.insight: Defense News reported Friday from Kyiv that Washington blamed Moscow at the United Nations on Wednesday for moving Russian military satellite Cosmos 2612 close to ICEYE-X36, a U.S.-registered radar satellite the paper says is believed to serve Ukraine. Officials said they would defend American interests in space. The piece does not quote a new treaty.

culture.hed: Providence reviews a career-long history of seapower and the societies that built it
culture.insight: Thursday's Providence essay by Thomas Sheppard reviews British historian N.A.M. Rodger's attempt to write a complete history of seapower across a career. Sheppard sets the book against the older 'new military history' that put armies in the context of the societies that raised them. It is a review. It does not report a new deployment.
